_why: Which flash sources are under the register today, and what each worst case must show to count as played. check-log.js reads it. `reserved` are the sources Rendering's docs/rendering/flash-sources.md names for the register: when one asks, it appears in the logs and is reported as counted; until then it is reported UNCOUNTED. `outside` are sources nothing asks for. A source in a log that is in neither `counted` nor `reserved` is a problem until it is added here.

reservedNotes.body_hit: Rendering: the whole body white for 0.12 s on every hit (fighter_view.gd); the largest strobe risk at a mash's hit rate. Counted here by proxy from the sim's hurt time, and by the pixel analyser.
reservedNotes.head_flash: Rendering: 2 or 3 icon pulses at the head (flash_view.gd); one pulse in reduced motion. Pixels only.
reservedNotes.guard_flash: Rendering: the guard arc flaring on a perfect block. Pixels only.
reservedNotes.cue_flare: Rendering: a soft glow at the chest on four of Combat's cue poses. Pixels only.
reservedNotes.beam: Rendering: a signature beam's white core (beam_view.gd): one bright step up and one down. Pixels only.
reservedNotes.beam_clash: Rendering: the flare where two beams meet (beam_view.gd). Pixels only.

outside.divider_slam: Camera's and UI's: the split divider's slam flash. Not Rendering's or VFX's; no register ask; pixels only.
outside.glare: VFX's glare on the rival's glasses: steady for its hold, not a flash; listed so a reader knows it was considered.
outside.recharge_ring: UI's launch marks (Legal RL-143, fx04): the plate's recharging ring, one step a second (1 Hz), a stroke with no brightness change. In every frame of the pixel set; the analyser reads it. Not a register ask.
outside.tug_ring: UI's beam struggle tug ring (Legal RL-143, fx04): closes on the 20-tick pulse (3 Hz), strokes only, steady under Reduce flashing and Reduced motion. In every frame of the pixel set; the analyser reads it. Not a register ask.

pairings._why: AI matches of the launch pair, full length, in both modes. 12345, 4 and 7 are hash_check's seeds (12345 and 4 failed the first pixel gate); 1, 3, 5, 38 and 39 were chosen by tools/flash/seed_scan.gd so that both fighters fire their signature across the set (PROTAGONIST in 1, 3, 5, 38, 39; RIVAL in 4, 7, 1, 5, 39), with a beam clash (most), a guard (5, 38), a deflect (39) and a city collapse (3, 5, 39), and so that the staged run raises no script error (seeds 17 and 19 were dropped: they raise 670 and 794 errors in sim/world/collateral.gd, see docs/tools/flash-check.md). Re-picked with the dummy in the roster: 20 seeds in all across three pairings; the failed seeds of earlier candidates (4, 39, 104, 106) and the five worst of the previous release stay.

The training dummy (the reference fighter, in the roster as Simulation's dummy_roster.py puts him): AI matches of a launch fighter against him, full length, both modes; picked by tools/flash/pick-seeds.mjs (Legal's RL-131: a pairing new in a release at least 3 times, every fighter in at least 5 matches).

The training dummy (the reference fighter, in the roster as Simulation's dummy_roster.py puts him): AI matches of a launch fighter against him, full length, both modes; picked by tools/flash/pick-seeds.mjs (Legal's RL-131: a pairing new in a release at least 3 times, every fighter in at least 5 matches).

_pairings: The fixed list of AI matches the pixel gate must pass (Legal, RL-119). One entry for every unordered pair of distinct fighters in data/fighters/roster.json (slots in roster order; selftest.js fails when the roster has a pair this list lacks), each with seeds that between them show every fighter of the pair firing its signature (check-log.js checks it from the runs' events). Add an entry when a fighter joins the roster.
